entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Zheng Guo was a Chinese hydraulic engineer who lived towards the end of the Warring States period (370–256 BCE).

Born into a family of modest means in the state of Zhao, Zheng Guo's expertise in water management and engineering soon made him a sought-after consultant for various states. His most notable achievement was the design and construction of the Zhengguo Canal, a 150 km long waterway that connected the Yellow River to the Wei River, significantly enhancing the agricultural productivity of the region.

The Zhengguo Canal had a profound impact on the development of Chinese water management systems, and its design was studied and emulated by subsequent engineers for centuries. Although the exact details of his life are not well documented, Zheng Guo's contributions to the field of hydraulic engineering remain an important part of China's rich cultural heritage.

The legacy of Zheng Guo can be seen in the many water management systems that continue to be used in China today, a testament to the enduring impact of his innovative designs.
